quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Get back at the other driver by cutting them off.

questions.explanation: Don't take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps avoid road rage and accidents.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires cause problems. They increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and cause hydroplaning. All of these are serious safety risks.

questions.question: To practice defensive driving, you should:

options.text: Be aware of developing traffic situations around you.
Look ahead of your vehicle and keep a safe following distance.
Have a backup plan ready for unexpected events.
All of the above

questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead and watching for problems. Keep a safe distance from other cars and be ready with a backup plan. This helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: You are driving in moderate traffic on a four-lane highway behind a slow-moving vehicle. Before changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Signal for at least 100 feet.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure there is enough room in traffic for your move.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Make sure there is enough space and you won't force other drivers to change their speed.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Stops the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably across your chest with room for one fist between the belt and your body.

questions.question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden move to reach your exit. Just continue driving and take the next exit instead.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Doing all three keeps you and others safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a multilane highway and wish to change lanes. You must signal your intentions:

options.text: Right before changing lanes.
Only during the lane change.
At least 50 feet before changing lanes.
At least 100 feet before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 100 feet before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you start to change lanes. That's about the length of five cars. Signal even longer when driving faster.

questions.question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to approach.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel when a police officer stops you. Ask passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must produce:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
A driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents must be in your car when you drive.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic rules instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to do so. Not following a flagger's directions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: A driver who is taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings before you drive. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether you can drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you find a safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you find a safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder or lane is illegal.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Ease your foot off the gas and do not brake until you have control. Once the car is under control, brake gently and pull off the road at a safe spot.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another car could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Make no mistakes.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous because you must take one hand off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting. Before moving right or left, quickly look over your shoulder to check if your blind spot is clear.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Let other drivers know what you are doing to help prevent accidents.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: When you take alcohol with another drug, the effects of both can become stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine could affect you like you have had several drinks.

questions.question: If you change your name, you must tell the county examiner of drivers within how many days?

options.text: 60 days
20 days
10 days
30 days

questions.explanation: You must tell the county examiner of drivers about a name change within 30 days. You must do this in person and bring proof of the change.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you and a car on your right arrive at the same time. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection
Slow down and let the car on your right go first
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop
Honk your horn and drive through

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right of way. Wait until that car passes safely before you go.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Go through if there is no traffic coming
Keep driving because you have the right of way
Stop only if a police officer is nearby
Come to a complete stop

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You can turn right on red only if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive
The road is slippery when wet
The road curves ahead
A hill is coming

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night
You cannot see as well in the dark
It rains more at night
You see more motorcycles at night

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far or as clearly. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn, yield on green
One-way
Cattle crossing
Two-way left turn

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to yield to oncoming traffic when turning left at a green light. You can complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When another driver is acting angry, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid making eye contact with them
Do not make hand gestures at them
Stay away from them
Do all of these

questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, do everything you can to stay away from them. Avoid looking at them or making gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red
Keep driving because you have the right of way
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection
Look at what the other cars are doing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming next. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection, you may go through.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming
Look both ways before crossing
Always come to a complete stop
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection and let other cars and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks safely?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing
Listen and look both ways, then go if it is safe
Cross quickly when a train is coming
Go quickly under the lowering gates

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then go if it is safe
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look both ways for trains coming from either direction. Do not cross until you are sure it is safe.
